text:
The Penguins were being scouted as much as they were playing. Elliotte Friedman reported Saturday that the Senators have interest in Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell, and Ottawa general manager Steve Staios was in the building in Nashville to watch. What he saw was Pittsburgh build a two-goal lead and lose it, 4-3, to a Predators team that has been one of November's best stories.

Pittsburgh started well. Samuel Girard scored on a slap shot less than four minutes in, with Sidney Crosby picking up an assist, and Andrei Kuzmenko made it 2-0 late in the first. Then Jonathan Marchessault beat Sergei Murashov on a slap shot our numbers gave a 2% chance, and Nashville took control. Filip Forsberg tied it early in the second, and Reid Schaefer gave the Predators a 3-2 lead. Hendrix Lapierre answered for Pittsburgh at 13:23 of the second to make it 3-3.

The winner came from the blue line. Jayden Struble, set up by Steven Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly, scored 3:31 into the third on a 26% chance, the best look of any goal on the night, and Nashville's win chances jumped from 52% to 78%. Struble finished with a goal and an assist and the first star. Juuse Saros then made the stop that mattered, on Rutger McGroarty's 21% chance in the third.

The Predators earned it. They had 3.37 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to Pittsburgh's 2.08, and 1.6 of those came in the third period. Our replays gave Nashville the win 60% of the time. Neither goalie was sharp: Saros allowed a goal more than his shots deserved and Murashov 1.4 more.

For Nashville, this fits the month. The Predators ran off seven straight wins earlier in November and Saros has been in the Vezina conversation; even a Penguins writer, Ryan Wilson, was moved to call this group's run a "Last Stand." Pittsburgh is heading the other way. The trade headlines now cover Crosby, Erik Karlsson, Evgeni Malkin and Rakell, and a night like this, when a two-goal lead disappears in front of a rival general manager, won't quiet them.
headline: Struble finishes Nashville's comeback against selling Penguins
